title.narrative: Strengthening Access to Protection Services for GBV Survivors and Vulnerable Children in Bama and Ngala LGAs of Borno State (SAFE-GUARD)

description.narrative: ltpgtThe SAFE-GUARD project, formally titled “Strengthening Access to Protection Services for GBV Survivors and Vulnerable Children in Bama and Ngala LGAs of Borno State,” will be implemented by the Gender Equality, Peace and Development Centre (GEPaDC) with technical supervision and mentorship from FHI 360. The project focuses on improving access to critical protection services for survivors of Gender-Based Violence (GBV) and vulnerable children in the conflict-affected communities of Bama and Ngala LGAs in Borno State, Nigeria.ltbrgtThe project integrates GBV response and prevention, Child Protection (CP), including protection from sexual exploitation and abuse. Coordination with humanitarian partners and government actors will ensure strengthened referral mechanisms, improved case management systems, and more inclusive, accountable service delivery mechanisms. A key emphasis is placed on building local resilience and capacity to respond to protection risks sustainably.ltbrgtUnder the GBV component, SAFE-GUARD will establish and operate Women and Girls Safe Spaces (WGSS), provide psychosocial support (PSS), conduct safety audits, and implement GBV risk mitigation activities. Awareness will be promoted through Information, Education, and Communication (IEC) materials and community advocacy events such as the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence and the Day of the Girl Child. Staff and community volunteers will also receive capacity-building support to enhance prevention and response efforts. Protection from sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA) activities, such as monitoring and the establishment of community-based mechanisms (CBMs), will be conducted during the project implementation in Bama and Ngala. GBV coordination and mainstreaming will be integrated in sectors and ensure appropriate coordination and referral mechanisms.ltbrgtIn Ngala LGA, the Child Protection component will deliver case management training, psychosocial support, including Psychological First Aid (PFA), and assistance for child survivors of sexual violence. It will also support the reintegration of at-risk children and strengthen community-based CP coordination, community awareness, and psychosocial recreational activities that aid in strengthening a protective environment for children and their caregivers. Protection monitoring activities will be led by community-based Protection Committees, who will identify risks, document incidents, and alert humanitarian actors. All data will be disaggregated by age, gender, disability, and displacement status to ensure inclusivity and relevance.ltbrgtThe project will directly benefit 5,000 individuals and indirectly reach approximately 10,000 people across the two LGAs. Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) will be central, with mechanisms for safe feedback and participatory monitoring. Sustainability will be ensured by building local capacity, ltbrgtintegrating systems into government-led services and providing mentorship throughout the implementation process. lt/pgtltpgtOverall, the SAFE-GUARD project aligns with the Nigeria Humanitarian Fund (NHF) priorities and global standards on GBV/PSEA mainstreaming, Child Protection, and AAP, aiming to foster a safer, more inclusive, and resilient environment for women, girls, boys, and other vulnerable populations.ltbrgtlt/pgt
